mutants.why: An integration test's httpapi.Deps literal omits the required Payment, which only CI's integration run would otherwise catch at runtime.
The new-module characterization template omits the required Stats in its httpapi.Deps literal, so every generated module would fail at runtime.
Send treats every request as new, so a resend no longer returns the first message and the conflict path never finds it.
A resend with the same request_id but different content is no longer rejected with InvalidInput on RequestID.
The resend lookup stops keying on the sender side, so the store's message with the buyer's request_id is treated as a resend of the buyer's message.

A request_id conflict no longer rolls the transaction back: the loser commits its allocated seq and returns an empty message, so the loser's response differs from the winner's and last_seq runs ahead of the stored messages (race-dependent: needs the concurrent duplicates to collide).
ConversationParties returns the buyer and store the wrong way round.
Presence stops restricting the batch to conversations owned by the caller, so another party's conversation is answered instead of failing the whole request with NotFound.

The request_id is validated but never handed to the module, so a resend is no longer idempotent.
A hidden or erased message carries its text and image again when the module returns content for it.

mutants.why: before_seq and after_seq are accepted together instead of invalid_argument.
The declared capability for the store sending a message no longer matches the capability the module checks.
A httpapi.Deps literal in the module template omits the required IM field, which must fail the literals guard.
The stream never calls Guard on the recheck tick, so a revoked session or closed store keeps the stream open until its lifetime ends.
Every stream gets exactly MaxLifetime, so streams opened together reconnect together.
Frames are written without a per-write deadline, so a client that stops reading holds the connection forever.
Transient recheck failures accumulate across successes, so three scattered blips end a healthy stream.
A single transient recheck failure ends the stream instead of three consecutive ones.

A Send joined to an outer transaction retries after a request_id conflict, running more SQL in a transaction the conflict did not roll back and leaving a seq gap.

mutants.why: A resend of a hidden message returns its content with hidden=false instead of the tombstone.
A resend of an erased text message compares against the erased (empty) content and is rejected as InvalidInput instead of returning the tombstone.
When a server fails on its own, Run's context is cancelled only after Shutdown, so open streams do not end through Run and Shutdown waits out its timeout.
Blocking a conversation's store through message_id fails with not_found when the store has no StoreCard, although such a store can hold a conversation.
An explicit before_seq of 0 reaches the module as 0 and returns the latest page instead of an empty one.

A store stream whose store is gone or replaced ends as unauthenticated instead of failed_precondition STORE_CLOSED.
A chat handler without Reads starts and fails on the first request.
Any UUID version with a valid variant is accepted as a request_id.
